title: Testing Across Operating Systems knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Testing Across Operating Systems?
options: An OS matrix catches platform-specific paths, shell, filesystem, and behavior differences on supported runners.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: An OS matrix catches platform-specific paths, shell, filesystem, and behavior differences on supported runners.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of testing across operating systems: An OS matrix catches platform-specific paths, shell, filesystem, and behavior differences on supported runners. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to testing across operating systems?
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: An OS matrix catches platform-specific paths, shell, filesystem, and behavior differences on supported runners. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
